title: Hister
name: hister
description: Search engine for your own browsing history. A browser extension sends every page you visit to it, and you search the full text of everything you've read, with previews, rules for what gets kept and an MCP server for AI tools. Source: https://github.com/asciimoo/hister

env.name: HISTER_TOKEN
env.label: Access token (required)
env.description: What you'll log in with, and what the browser extension sends. Generate one with: openssl rand -hex 32

env.name: HISTER_URL
env.label: Address you'll open it on (required)
env.description: Exactly what you'll type in the browser, port included and no slash at the end, like http://192.168.1.20:4433

env.name: HISTER_PORT
env.label: Host port for the web UI

note: Set the access token (openssl rand -hex 32 makes a good one) and the address before you deploy, since the stack won't start without both. The address has to be exactly what you type in the browser, like http://192.168.1.20:4433, with the same port as the host port field. Get it wrong and the page still loads, but search just says "Cannot connect to Hister", so fix the address and update the stack. Then open it and sign in with the token as the password. To fill it, install the Hister extension for Firefox or Chrome and give it the same address and token. Pages are only indexed from then on, and importing your old history is done with the hister command line tool. Everything, the index and settings included, lives in the hister-data volume. Docs: hister.org/docs
